evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: Practice: mothers of infants in six villages of Udaipur district, Rajasthan, bring the child to the monthly immunization camp for the third DPT dose in the month it is due. We want more of it. Our ASHAs say 'nobody here goes back after the first shots', but the camp register shows 46% of infants due got the third dose. Last month we interviewed 22 mothers alone at home, picked from the register (11 whose child got the third dose, 11 whose child did not), and held 2 group discussions with mothers-in-law. What we heard: 17 of 22 mothers said the later shots are good for the child. Asked how many of ten mothers in their lane go back, most said 'three or four'. 14 said their mother-in-law or the older women in the lane think the shots bring fever, and that a child with fever after a shot shows a careless mother. Four mothers who went back said they were told 'you want to show you are better than us'. Asked whether they would go if most mothers in the lane went, 15 said yes, 4 said they go anyway, 3 said no because of the fever. In the groups the mothers-in-law said the shots are 'fine, the nurse says so'. The practice is not sensitive. Is this a social norm?
evals.expected_output: A social norm diagnosis in the output template that makes a provisional call and says what would confirm it.
assertions: Sorts the mothers' answers under the four questions, with the counts given.
Does not treat the ASHAs' statement or the 46% figure as evidence of a norm.
Shows each branch of the classification, marks the call provisional, and drafts no message or declaration.
Flags that the mothers-in-law, speaking in groups, may have given the official answer.
Lists the belief about fever as something else holding the practice in place.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Is open defecation a social norm in our villages?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the practice, what the people concerned have said, and whether the practice is sensitive, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks who does what, when, and what the program wants.
Asks what people who follow the practice have said, or whether anything has been collected.
Does not classify the practice.
Does not invent respondents' answers.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We work in three woredas in Amhara, Ethiopia, on child marriage. Practice: parents arrange a marriage for a daughter before she turns 18. We want less of it. Nothing has been collected yet. We plan to run your four questions in mixed village meetings next month with parents, elders, and the girls themselves, about 40 people per meeting, and ask who in the village still arranges early marriages and what happens to families who refuse. Can you give us the question set and the diagnosis plan?
evals.expected_output: The skill gives the four questions marked pending field answers, says the mixed meetings are not a safe setting, and names the specialists to consult before anyone is asked.
assertions: Gives the four questions for this practice and marks the call "pending field answers".
Says mixed village meetings are not a safe setting for these questions.
Includes no question that asks people to name families who arrange or refuse early marriages.
Names a local qualitative researcher who knows the practice and an ethics reviewer, to consult before anyone is asked.
Says what to bring to them.
Makes no classification.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We already did the diagnosis: in our 12 villages in East Nusa Tenggara, open defecation is a social norm, people underestimate how many neighbors have built latrines, and the people they watch are the neighbors in the same hamlet. Now write us the noticeboard message saying most households have already built a latrine.
evals.expected_output: The skill says the diagnosis exists and the request is for a message, and points to the skill that writes it.
assertions: Says the request is to write a norm message, not to diagnose.
Names write-social-norm-message.
Does not classify the practice again.
Produces no message text.
